notes:
Account background: mid-market analytics SaaS (B2B) building in-product assistant for onboarding and support.

Why engaged: migrating away from incumbent (OpenAI) after multiple latency regressions in December–January impacted live chat SLAs. Product team prioritized stable streaming and robust tool-calling for actions (search, rerank, ticket creation).

Recent conversations: AE intro (11/12) -> product demo (11/19) -> security call (12/02) -> benchmarking kickoff (01/08). Currently in active evaluation of Hosted API with view to Dedicated if throughput/SLOs require it.

Benchmarking notes (internal):
- Goal: P95 token-to-token streaming latency <= 300ms under production-like load; end-to-end agent action (tool call + external API) P95 <= 800ms.
- Redwood streaming (internal perf run 02/10): median token latency 120–220ms depending on sequence length; P95 steady-state ~260–310ms.
- Incumbent (OpenAI) run (02/10): median 300–420ms; P95 spikes to 800–1400ms during burst windows — primary reason customer flagged regressions.
- Tool-calling: Redwood hosted POC with mock ticket-creation hook completed full roundtrip P95 520ms vs incumbent ~1.2s. Team: "noticeably smoother streaming, fewer reconnects" (quote from Eng lead).
- Cost: preliminary unit cost comparable; customer cares about predictable billing under sustained concurrency — interested in Dedicated pricing for committed throughput.

POC ask from customer:
- 2-week POC using Hosted API (streaming + tool calling) integrated into staging chat flow.
- Synthetic traffic: 100 concurrent users, 30 RPS sustained, mixture of short/long sessions.
- Clear test checklist: latency SLOs, reconnect/resume behavior, token accounting visibility, failure/fallback scoring.

Security/compliance: customer requires SSO (SAML), audit logs for model requests, KMS for key management, and optional EU data residency for EU customers. Legal preparing data residency addendum.

Sales/ops notes: introduced Dedicated conversation once POC shows <350ms P95 at target load. Finance wants committed TCO vs hosted consumption threshold at ~200k tokens/mo.

Customer quote from benchmarking review (02/18): "If Redwood keeps these streaming numbers under load, moving from hosted to reserved capacity makes sense — we need predictability more than lowest per-token price."
